subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI VISUAL/EDITOR compose handoff now, and what trigger plus temp-file/process guardrails should govern it?
rationale: The feature is coherent and still missing, but it launches a local editor process and temporarily persists prompt contents outside the in-memory composer, so automation should not choose the UX and security boundary alone.

options.title: Approve Bounded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the chosen shortcut or slash command with TUI suspension, VISUAL/EDITOR draft round trip, no auto-submit, explicit error states, privacy/cleanup docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Require Design First
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers settle shortcut conflicts, slash-command discoverability, temp-file lifetime, and privacy wording.

options.title: Defer Editor Handoff
options.body: Leave long-prompt ergonomics to inline multiline, vi-mode, or web composer improvements and decline local editor process launch for now.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the chosen shortcut or slash command with TUI suspension, VISUAL/EDITOR draft round trip, no auto-submit, explicit error states, privacy/cleanup docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from the prior issue review, TUI source history, and current-line ownership in this area.
